S21.01.note: The plan's line 191 is stale; the header is pushed in the Event::Start(Tag::CodeBlock) arm of markdown_renderer.rs. The header is drawn in the chat transcript, not a separate panel.
steps: Run `agi` in a terminal and sign in if asked.
Type "Show a Rust hello world in a code block" and press Enter.
When the reply arrives, look at the top edge of the code block.
Compare: the header line reads ┌─ rust ─ (the language name), or ┌─ code ─ when the fence has no language.
S21.01.where: agi (start the app), then type a request that gets a code block back, e.g. "Show a Rust hello world in a code block"

S21.02.note: Colours depend on the terminal palette; the code only shows that highlight_code runs syntect for the fence language.
steps: Run `agi` in a terminal.
Type "Show a Python function in a code block" and press Enter.
When the reply arrives, compare the code's keywords, strings and comments in the block.
Compare: keywords, strings and numbers show in different colours (the highlighter is syntect, chosen by language); a block with no language shows as plain text.
S21.02.where: agi (start the app), then type a request that gets a code block back, e.g. "Show a Python function in a code block"

S21.03.note: There is no per-block copy button; /copy code copies the most recent code block only. If the clipboard is unavailable, the app prints the contents instead.
steps: Run `agi` and ask for a reply that contains a code block.
Type /copy code and press Enter.
Read the message line: it should say "Copied last code block to clipboard" with a line count.
Paste (Cmd-V) into a text editor and compare with the block: only the code, no fences or the text around it.
S21.03.where: agi (start the app), then type /copy code at the prompt

S21.09.needs: a git repository with changed files
S21.09.note: No separate code-suggestion highlight was found; changed lines are highlighted in the diff review and in edit results.
steps: Run `agi` in a git repository where a file has unsaved changes.
Type /diff-review and press Enter.
Read the "Diff Review" panel; added and removed lines are drawn on coloured bands.
Compare: added lines and removed lines are visibly coloured differently. Also ask the agent to edit a file and check the + and - counts and coloured lines under the tool row.
S21.09.where: agi (start the app), then type /diff-review at the prompt

S21.10.needs: a git repository with changed files
S21.10.note: The +/- prefixes come from apps/cli/src/diff_model.rs and the hunk header format is there too.
steps: Run `agi` in a git repository with changes.
Type /diff-review and press Enter.
Use the arrow keys to move between files and hunks.
Compare: each hunk has an @@ header line, added lines start with +, removed lines start with -, and they are coloured. /diff also prints a summary.
S21.10.where: agi (start the app), then type /diff-review at the prompt

S21.12.needs: a folder you can run commands in
S21.12.note: Running is done by the agent's run_command tool, not by a control on code blocks; it runs on the local shell after approval, and the sandbox mode decides what it may touch. Not found: a sandbox option for code execution.
steps: Run `agi` in a folder you are happy for commands to run in.
Type "Run `echo hello` in the shell" and press Enter.
When the approval box appears, read the command shown and press y (Yes).
Compare: a tool row named run_command shows the command with $ and then prints its output. There is no run button on the code block itself.
S21.12.where: agi (start the app), then ask the agent in the prompt to run a command, e.g. "Run `echo hello` in the shell"

labels.text: showing full tool output, Ctrl-O to collapse

S21.15.needs: a folder you can run commands in
S21.15.note: The output is inline under the tool row, not a separate panel; expanded output is capped at 200 lines.
steps: Run `agi` and ask "Run `ls` in the shell" and approve it with y.
Look at the lines printed under the run_command row.
Press Ctrl-O to show the full output.
Compare: output shows indented under the tool row (a preview first), and Ctrl-O shows full output with the note "showing full tool output, Ctrl-O to collapse".
S21.15.where: agi (start the app), then ask the agent to run a command that prints several lines

S21.16.needs: a folder you can run commands in
S21.16.note: Only the first stderr line shows until Ctrl-O is pressed.
steps: Run `agi` and send the request above, approving it with y.
Look under the run_command row for a line starting with "stderr".
Compare: the stderr label and text are drawn in the danger colour and bold, so they differ from the stdout lines.
Press Ctrl-O to see more stderr lines if there are several.
S21.16.where: agi (start the app), then ask the agent to run a command that fails, e.g. "Run `ls /no-such-folder` in the shell"

S21.18.needs: a folder you can run commands in
steps: Run `agi` and send the request above, approving it with y.
Look at the end of the run_command row.
Compare: a failing command shows "exit 1" (or its code) in red, and a passing command shows "exit 0" in green, with a ✗ or ✔ glyph at the start of the row.
S21.18.where: agi (start the app), then ask the agent to run a command that fails, e.g. "Run `false` in the shell"

S21.19.needs: a folder you can run commands in
S21.19.note: Searched apps/cli for open, download and output-file controls. The app lists "Files changed this turn" (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs) and shows edits, but found no control to open or download files a command produced.

S21.22.needs: a folder you can run commands in
S21.22.note: The code shows Esc and Ctrl-C stop the turn; whether the underlying shell process is killed was not traced.
steps: Run `agi` and send the request above, approving it with y.
While the turn is running, read the status line: "working, Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel".
Press Esc (or Ctrl-C).
Compare: the turn stops and the run_command row is marked cancelled (⊘) or failed, and the prompt comes back.
S21.22.where: agi (start the app), then ask for a long-running command, e.g. "Run `sleep 60` in the shell"

S21.27.note: The approval box only allows the change after its detail has been scrolled to the end, per the overlay's own docs.
steps: Run `agi` in a repository and send the request above.
When the "Apply this patch?" approval box appears, read the file names and the change.
Press y to apply, or n to refuse.
Compare: the file changes on disk and the tool row shows +N -N. To review changes later, type /diff-review and press y to approve a hunk or n to reject it.
S21.27.where: agi (start the app), then ask the agent to change a file, e.g. "Add a comment line to README.md"

labels.text: Run it this once. Tab adds a note for the agent.

S21.29.needs: a folder with files; default permission mode (not Bypass)
S21.29.note: The box shows the command and what it touches; the Bypass mode skips the box, so the tester must be outside Bypass.
steps: Run `agi` in a folder with files, in the default permission mode (press Shift+Tab until the mode is the normal chat mode, not Bypass).
Type "Run `ls` in the shell" and press Enter.
Read the approval box: the command is shown, and the buttons are Yes, No, Allow Session, Always allow, Deny All, Allow All.
Move to Yes and compare the text that appears: "Run it this once. Tab adds a note for the agent."
S21.29.where: agi (start the app), then ask the agent to run a command, e.g. "Run `ls` in the shell"
